## Read AI code one line at a time {#read-ai data-hold="true"}

```{=html}
<div class="annot" id="annot">
  <ol class="annot-code" aria-label="Code lines; choose one to see what it assumes">
    <li><button type="button" data-i="0"><span>df = pd.read_csv("my_air_quality.csv", sep=";",</span><span>decimal=",", na_values=[-200])</span></button></li>
    <li><button type="button" data-i="1"><span>df = df.drop_duplicates()</span></button></li>
    <li><button type="button" data-i="2"><span>df = df.dropna(how="all")</span></button></li>
    <li><button type="button" data-i="3"><span>print(df["CO(GT)"].isna().sum())</span></button></li>
    <li><button type="button" data-i="4"><span>print(df["CO(GT)"].mean())</span></button></li>
  </ol>
  <div class="annot-card" aria-live="polite">
    <p class="annot-hint" id="annot-hint">Choose a line. For each one, ask two questions.</p>
    <div id="annot-body" hidden>
      <p class="label">What this line assumes about the file</p><p id="annot-a"></p>
      <p class="label">How you check it</p><p id="annot-c"></p>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
<script>
(function () {
  const root = document.getElementById('annot'); if (!root) return;
  root.addEventListener('click', (e) => e.stopPropagation());
  const N = [
    ['Columns are split by a semicolon, the decimal mark is a comma, and −200 means missing in every column, not only in CO.',
     'Look at df.dtypes: every measurement column should be float64, not object. Count missing values per column with df.isna().sum().'],
    ['A row that repeats exactly is an error in the export, not two real hours with identical readings.',
     'Count rows before and after. You should be able to say which rows were removed and why.'],
    ['A row with no values at all carries no information and can be removed.',
     'Count rows again. Only the empty rows at the end of the file should go.'],
    ['Nothing new. It reports how many CO hours are missing, which the next line silently skips.',
     'The count should match what you saw in the raw file. A count of 0 means the missing code was not declared.'],
    ['The mean of the hours that are left describes the whole two weeks.',
     'Ask which days those hours come from. If the analyzer was off for four days, the mean describes ten days, not fourteen.'],
  ];
  const btns = root.querySelectorAll('.annot-code button');
  btns.forEach((b) => b.addEventListener('click', () => {
    btns.forEach((o) => o.setAttribute('aria-pressed', o === b));
    const [a, c] = N[+b.dataset.i];
    document.getElementById('annot-hint').hidden = true;
    document.getElementById('annot-body').hidden = false;
    document.getElementById('annot-a').textContent = a;
    document.getElementById('annot-c').textContent = c;
  }));
})();
</script>
```

[This version declares the missing code. It can still mislead: see the last line.]{.note-line}

::: {.prompt .small}
Same file as Session 1: 336 hours, repeated and empty rows already removed, 99 CO hours at −200. Before you reveal anything: which code goes into the 09:00 report? For the other two, name the check that catches them.
:::

::: {.selfstudy}
Studying alone: write your choice and two checks, then reveal.
:::

## What each one prints, and why {#act1-answer}

| Code | Prints | What happened | The check that catches it |
|--|----|----------------------|----------------------|
| A | nan | NMHC(GT) is −200 in all 336 hours, so dropna() removes every row | Count rows after each step: 0 |
| B | 1.93 | Each of the 99 missing hours enters the mean as 0.0 mg/m³ | Count zeros, or look at the minimum: a clean-air zero every time the analyzer was off |
| C | 99 and 2.74 | −200 is declared missing; the mean skips the 99 hours | The count matches the raw file; the minimum is above 0 |

[A runs without an error and prints nothing useful. B prints a plausible number. B is the more dangerous one.]{.note-line}

[Data: S. De Vito, Air Quality, UCI Machine Learning Repository, doi:10.24432/C59K5F, CC BY 4.0. Window: 18 Dec 2004 02:00 to 1 Jan 2005 01:00.]{.source}

::: {.bridge}
One hour of the day loses CO far more often than the rest. A mean of the valid hours under-weights 04:00. Treating −200 as missing is necessary; it does not make the remaining hours a fair sample.
:::

[Share of hours with CO(GT) = −200, all 9,357 hours, March 2004 to April 2005. The source does not say why. Data: De Vito, UCI, doi:10.24432/C59K5F, CC BY 4.0.]{.source}

## When is a daily mean worth reporting? {#reportable data-hold="true"}

```{=html}
<div class="rep" id="rep">
  <label class="sm-slider">Minimum valid hours per day <strong id="rep-k">18 h</strong>
    <input type="range" id="rep-min" min="1" max="24" step="1" value="18">
  </label>
  <div class="rep-days" id="rep-days"></div>
  <p class="rep-out" id="rep-out" aria-live="polite"></p>
</div>
<script>
(function () {
  const root = document.getElementById('rep'); if (!root) return;
  root.addEventListener('click', (e) => e.stopPropagation());
  // Same window as Activity 1: [day, hours in file, valid CO hours, mean of valid CO hours]
  const D = [["18 Dec",22,22,1.76],["19 Dec",24,23,2.73],["20 Dec",24,24,2.36],["21 Dec",24,24,2.03],["22 Dec",24,23,2.22],
             ["23 Dec",24,24,4.06],["24 Dec",24,24,5.32],["25 Dec",24,23,3.92],["26 Dec",24,24,1.43],["27 Dec",24,24,1.57],
             ["28 Dec",24,1,1.2],["29 Dec",24,0,null],["30 Dec",24,0,null],["31 Dec",24,0,null],["01 Jan",2,1,1.6]];
  const input = document.getElementById('rep-min');
  function draw() {
    const k = +input.value; document.getElementById('rep-k').textContent = k + ' h';
    let html = '', n = 0;
    for (const [day, hrs, ok] of D) {
      const kept = ok >= k; if (kept) n++;
      html += '<div class="rep-day ' + (ok === 0 ? 'none' : kept ? 'kept' : 'short') + '"><b>' + ok + '</b><span>' + day + '</span></div>';
    }
    document.getElementById('rep-days').innerHTML = html;
    const kept = D.filter((d) => d[2] >= k);
    const mean = kept.length ? (kept.reduce((s, d) => s + d[3], 0) / kept.length).toFixed(2) : '–';
    document.getElementById('rep-out').innerHTML = '<b>' + n + ' of 15</b> days reported · mean of reported daily means <b>' + mean + ' mg/m³</b> · the single two-week mean is 2.74';
  }
  input.addEventListener('input', draw); draw();
})();
</script>
```

::: {.bridge}
The file covers 15 calendar days. CO was measured on about ten. The 18-hour rule is an assumption for this lab, not a regulation; you will choose your own in Step 8b.
:::

[Numbers in each square: valid CO hours that day. Filled: reported. Open: below the minimum. Dashed: no valid hour.]{.source}
